# akeyless-watchover command reference (v1.6.0)

Two interfaces:

- **Skill commands** - typed to an AI agent that has the skill: `akeyless-watchover <command> [args]` (or the agent's skill syntax, e.g. `/akeyless-watchover`, `$akeyless-watchover`; MCP prompt `watchover-<command>`). Set-up per agent: [agents.md](agents.md).
- **Kit commands** - run in the governance repository: `scripts/watchover <command> [options]` (Python 3.10+ with pyyaml; Terraform >= 1.7 or OpenTofu >= 1.8; the akeyless CLI for live commands).

Notation: `<x>` required, `[x]` optional, `a|b` choice. *Live* = calls Akeyless.

## Skill commands

<a id="skill-help"></a>
### help

`akeyless-watchover help [command]`

**Does:** Show this guide, or the details of one skill command.  
**Delivers:** The command table, parameters and examples.

**How it works:**

- Reads references/usage-guide.md (or the command table in SKILL.md).
- With an argument, returns only that command's entry. Parameters are never invented.

**Example:** `/akeyless-watchover help design`

<a id="skill-design"></a>
### design

`akeyless-watchover design <diagram | description of BUs, apps, environments, personas>`

**Does:** Translate an organisation/structure diagram into Akeyless configuration.  
**Delivers:** Path tree, access matrix, YAML model (roles, auth methods, folders), access expectations, plan expectations, CLI equivalent.

**How it works:**

- Inventories BUs, applications, environments, data classes, personas and the identity source of each; asks for whatever is missing.
- Derives the path tree `/<bu>/<app>/<env>/...` (delegation boundary first, carve-outs such as `break-glass` as fixed segments) and the access matrix persona x scope.
- Creates one role per persona x scope x access level; binds humans through the SSO auth method + `groups` sub-claims and workloads through one auth method per trust boundary.
- Writes the model files and access_expectations.yaml, then runs `watchover simulate`/`test` when it can run commands.

**Example:** `/akeyless-watchover design <paste or attach the diagram>`

<a id="skill-change"></a>
### change

`akeyless-watchover change <access request in plain words>`

**Does:** Change existing access with the smallest possible model diff.  
**Delivers:** Diff of model/roles/<bu>.yaml (and auth_methods.yaml if needed), new expectations, who must approve (CODEOWNERS).

**How it works:**

- Finds the role file of the owning business unit (model/roles/<bu>.yaml).
- Applies the smallest change: a rule, an association, narrower sub-claims - or a new role when no existing role has the right audience.
- Adds a positive and a negative expectation, simulates, and lists the CODEOWNERS approvers.

**Example:** `/akeyless-watchover change give fraud-analysts read on /payments/+/prod/*`

<a id="skill-review"></a>
### review

`akeyless-watchover review <model files, merge-request diff or plan output>`

**Does:** Review a proposed change for least privilege, guard violations and blast radius.  
**Delivers:** Findings by severity, failing guards, missing expectations, plan red flags (replacements).

**How it works:**

- Checks the input against the guards, least privilege (root scope, removed deny rules, associations without sub-claims) and plan red flags (replacements caused by renames).
- Reports findings ranked by severity, with the missing expectations.

**Example:** `/akeyless-watchover review <paste the plan>`

<a id="skill-pipeline"></a>
### pipeline

`akeyless-watchover pipeline [github | gitlab] [repository]`

**Does:** Set up the governance repository: bootstrap identity, CI, CODEOWNERS, state.  
**Delivers:** bootstrap.tfvars, CI file, variables to create, step-by-step order.

**How it works:**

- Fills bootstrap.tfvars for the CI platform and repository, selects the CI template, lists the CI variables (masked or not) and the order of the steps.

**Example:** `/akeyless-watchover pipeline gitlab group/akeyless-governance`

<a id="skill-import"></a>
### import

`akeyless-watchover import [what to export: everything / a type / one user's view] [export directory or REPORT.md]`

**Does:** Export existing config (RBAC, auth methods incl. OIDC, folders, custom fields, key policies, PKI issuers, account settings) and translate it into Terraform.  
**Delivers:** The exact `watchover export` command (model or --hcl mode, filters), then resolution of every REPORT.md item and the import checklist until the plan shows imports only.

**How it works:**

- Chooses the export mode (model or --hcl) and filters, and gives the `watchover export` command.
- Reads REPORT.md and resolves every item (secrets, unsupported types, external references).
- Iterates until the plan shows imports only.

**Example:** `/akeyless-watchover import the OIDC auth method and everything alice@example.com can reach`

<a id="skill-reconcile"></a>
### reconcile

`akeyless-watchover reconcile [repository URL or checkout] [branch]`

**Does:** Compare the governance repository (GitHub Enterprise) with live Akeyless and prepare the changes for manual review. Never commits or pushes.  
**Delivers:** REPORT.md with every difference and its two resolutions, changes.patch, proposed files, imports.tf - to review and commit yourself.

**How it works:**

- Clones the repository read-only (or reads a checkout) and runs `watchover reconcile` with a read-only Akeyless identity; without a shell, gives the command to run.
- Explains each difference and asks whether Akeyless or the repository is right; adjusts the proposal (--only, --include-unmodelled, --propose-removals).
- Hands over the patch and files with the commands to apply and verify them (git apply, terraform plan). Never commits, pushes or opens a pull request.

**Example:** `akeyless-watchover reconcile https://ghe.example.com/platform/akeyless-governance main`

<a id="skill-conjur"></a>
### conjur

`akeyless-watchover conjur <Conjur policy YAML>`

**Does:** Migrate from CyberArk Conjur: secrets via the Gateway, RBAC via translation.  
**Delivers:** Translated roles, bindings to fill (auth method + sub-claims), migration resource, cut-over plan.

**How it works:**

- Runs or gives `watchover conjur`; proposes an auth method and sub-claims for each Conjur host and user in bindings.yaml; adds the Gateway migration entry and a cut-over plan.

**Example:** `/akeyless-watchover conjur <attach policy files>`

<a id="skill-pki"></a>
### pki

`akeyless-watchover pki <certificate requirements>`

**Does:** Design private/public CA issuers and who may request certificates.  
**Delivers:** pki.yaml (CA keys, issuers), requester roles, expiry forwarder, CLI to issue/revoke.

**How it works:**

- Writes pki.yaml (CA key, issuers: signer key or public CA target, domains, TTL, auto-renew), the requester roles, an expiry forwarder and the CLI to issue and revoke.

**Example:** `/akeyless-watchover pki internal TLS for *.payments.internal, 90 days, auto-renew`

<a id="skill-harden"></a>
### harden

`akeyless-watchover harden [current settings or concerns]`

**Does:** Account-level hardening.  
**Delivers:** governance.yaml: account_settings (Terraform), account_settings_cli (CLI), custom fields, key policies, event forwarders.

**How it works:**

- Splits the settings into the Terraform-managed subset (account_settings) and the CLI-only part (account_settings_cli); adds custom fields, key policies and critical event forwarders.
- Always starts with `watchover account-settings --dry-run`.

**Example:** `/akeyless-watchover harden`

<a id="skill-gateway"></a>
### gateway

`akeyless-watchover gateway <who administers which Gateway, SIEM target>`

**Does:** Gateway admin plane and audit-log forwarding.  
**Delivers:** gateway.yaml (allowed_access, log_forwarding), gateway_api setup.

**How it works:**

- Writes gateway.yaml: allowed_access (auth method or access ID + permissions) and log forwarding (syslog or splunk); sets gateway_api. One state per Gateway cluster.

**Example:** `/akeyless-watchover gateway platform admins full, PKI team targets only, Splunk`

<a id="skill-verify"></a>
### verify

`akeyless-watchover verify [persona | path]`

**Does:** Prove who can access what.  
**Delivers:** access_expectations.yaml checks, `watchover simulate` / `watchover verify` commands, Impersonate As steps.

**How it works:**

- Evaluates access with the Akeyless rules (wildcards, deny precedence, sub-claims OR within a key / AND across keys).
- Writes the matching expectation checks and the commands that prove them offline (`simulate`) and live (`verify`, Impersonate As).

**Example:** `/akeyless-watchover verify can the checkout pods read refunds prod?`

<a id="skill-cli"></a>
### cli

`akeyless-watchover cli <task>`

**Does:** Exact Akeyless CLI commands for a task (break-glass, bootstrap, one-off checks).  
**Delivers:** Commands checked against the CLI reference, with the equivalent model change.

**How it works:**

- Gives the exact `akeyless` commands, checked against the CLI reference, and the model change that makes the result permanent (CLI changes to roles are reverted by the next apply).

**Example:** `/akeyless-watchover cli create a temporary read rule for 60 minutes`

<a id="skill-explain"></a>
### explain

`akeyless-watchover explain <topic>`

**Does:** Explain an Akeyless concept precisely (sub-claims, deny, wildcards, anti-escalation...).  
**Delivers:** A short answer with the verified facts and VERIFY caveats.

**How it works:**

- Answers from the verified references; anything not confirmed by a primary source is marked VERIFY.

**Example:** `/akeyless-watchover explain should this run through the API or the CLI?`

## Kit commands

<a id="kit-test"></a>
### test

`scripts/watchover test [options]` - Run every offline check (what CI runs). *Offline.*

**How it works:**

- Runs, stopping at the first failure: fmt -check, init -backend=false, validate and `test` (mocked provider) in terraform/ and bootstrap/; guard_messages.sh (each negative fixture fails with the intended guard); export_roundtrip.sh; `simulate`; pytest.

| Option | Value | Required / default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--tool` | terraform/tofu | default terraform | IaC binary to use |
| `--skip-iac` | - | optional | only run the Python checks |

**Exit codes:** 0 all passed; otherwise the exit code of the first failing step

```bash
scripts/watchover test
scripts/watchover test --tool tofu
```

<a id="kit-simulate"></a>
### simulate

`scripts/watchover simulate [options]` - Offline: evaluate access_expectations.yaml against the model. *Offline.*

**How it works:**

- Loads model/roles/*.yaml and auth_methods.yaml.
- For each check: selects the roles whose associations match the persona's auth method and claims; collects the rules of the right type whose path pattern matches (claim templates expanded); a matching deny removes everything.
- Compares the resulting capability set with `expect` (exact match).

| Option | Value | Required / default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--model` | MODEL | required | model directory (terraform/model) |
| `--expectations` | EXPECTATIONS | required | access_expectations.yaml |
| `--explain` | - | optional | print the matching rules for every check, not only failures |

**Exit codes:** 0 all met; 1 mismatch; 2 model error

```bash
scripts/watchover simulate --model terraform/model --expectations terraform/model/access_expectations.yaml --explain
```

<a id="kit-verify"></a>
### verify

`scripts/watchover verify [options]` - Live: compare expectations with describe-permissions run as each persona's CLI profile. *Live.*

**How it works:**

- For each check whose persona has a `profile`: runs `akeyless describe-permissions --path --type --json --profile <persona>` and compares `client_permissions` with `expect`.
- Personas without a profile are skipped and counted.

| Option | Value | Required / default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--expectations` | EXPECTATIONS | required | access_expectations.yaml (personas need a 'profile') |
| `--akeyless` | AKEYLESS | default akeyless | path to the akeyless CLI binary |
| `--error-means-no-access` | - | optional | treat a failing describe-permissions call as 'no permissions' (check the CLI behaviour first) |

**Exit codes:** 0 all met; 1 mismatch; 2 CLI call failed

```bash
scripts/watchover verify --expectations terraform/model/access_expectations.yaml
```

<a id="kit-export"></a>
### export

`scripts/watchover export [options]` - Export existing config and translate it: YAML model + import blocks, or plain Terraform (--hcl). *Live.*

**How it works:**

- Reads the selected object families through the CLI (`--json`) or the REST API (token), following pagination; filters by name, root folder, depth or persona.
- Writes raw/ (JSON, secrets redacted) and REPORT.md (items needing a decision).
- Model mode: model/*.imported.yaml + imports.tf for the kit. --hcl: hcl/imports.tf with one import block per object; --generate runs `plan -generate-config-out` so Terraform writes the resources.

| Option | Value | Required / default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--out` | OUT | required | output directory (model/, imports.tf or hcl/, raw/, REPORT.md) |
| `--transport` | cli/api | default cli | how to read Akeyless: the akeyless CLI (profiles, SSO logins) or the REST API directly (token) |
| `--profile` | PROFILE | optional | cli transport: akeyless CLI profile with read access to the objects to export |
| `--akeyless` | AKEYLESS | default akeyless | cli transport: path to the akeyless CLI binary |
| `--gateway-url` | GATEWAY_URL | optional | cli transport, --types gateway: Gateway configuration URL (https://gw:8000) |
| `--api` | API | default https://api.akeyless.io | api transport: API base URL (default $AKEYLESS_API or https://api.akeyless.io) |
| `--token` | TOKEN | optional | api transport: Akeyless token (default $AKEYLESS_TOKEN; e.g. from 'watchover token') |
| `--gateway-api` | GATEWAY_API | optional | api transport, --types gateway: Gateway V2 API (https://gw:8000/api/v2) |
| `--from-dir` | FROM_DIR | optional | replay a raw/ directory of a previous export instead of calling the CLI |
| `--types` | TYPES | default roles,auth-methods,folders,custom-fields,key-policies,pki-issuers,account-settings,targets,groups | comma-separated object families (default: all but gateway): roles, auth-methods, folders, custom-fields, key-policies, pki-issuers, account-settings, targets, groups, gateway |
| `--only` | ONLY | optional | keep only objects whose name matches this regex |
| `--exclude` | EXCLUDE | repeatable | regex of names to skip (repeatable) |
| `--root` | ROOT | default / | folder to start the item/folder walk from |
| `--max-depth` | MAX_DEPTH | default 20 | maximum folder depth of the walk |
| `--persona-auth-method` | PERSONA_AUTH_METHOD | optional | keep one identity's view: its auth method ... |
| `--persona-claim` | PERSONA_CLAIM | repeatable | ... and its claims, key=value (repeatable); keeps roles whose association matches |
| `--hcl` | - | optional | write plain Terraform import blocks for every object (hcl/) |
| `--generate` | - | optional | with --hcl: run 'terraform plan -generate-config-out' (needs terraform and AKEYLESS_ACCESS_ID/AKEYLESS_ACCESS_KEY in the environment) |
| `--terraform` | TERRAFORM | default terraform | terraform or tofu binary used by --generate |

**Exit codes:** 0 written; 2 read/HTTP error or invalid options

```bash
scripts/watchover export --out export/ --profile admin --exclude '^/governance/auth/ci-terraform$'
scripts/watchover export --out export/ --profile admin --types auth-methods --only sso
scripts/watchover export --out export/ --profile admin --persona-auth-method /governance/auth/sso-entra-oidc --persona-claim email=alice@example.com --persona-claim groups=grp-akl-payments-admins
AKEYLESS_ACCESS_ID=p-... AKEYLESS_ACCESS_KEY=... scripts/watchover export --out export/ --profile admin --hcl --generate
AKEYLESS_TOKEN=$(scripts/watchover token) scripts/watchover export --out export/ --transport api --hcl --types targets,groups,gateway --gateway-api https://gw.example.com:8000/api/v2
scripts/watchover export --out export2/ --from-dir export/raw     # offline replay
```

<a id="kit-reconcile"></a>
### reconcile

`scripts/watchover reconcile [options]` - Compare the governance repository (e.g. GitHub Enterprise) with live Akeyless; write a report and a patch to review. Read-only: never commits or pushes. *Live.*

**How it works:**

- Gets the repository read-only: shallow clone of --ref with the push URL disabled, or reads --repo-dir as it is. Never writes to it, never commits or pushes.
- Exports roles, auth methods, folders, custom fields and key policies from Akeyless (as `export`; or uses --export-dir / --from-dir).
- Compares object by object after normalisation (defaults, ordering, *_var secret keys and guard switches ignored): changed, only in Akeyless, only in the repository.
- Writes REPORT.md, changes.patch (`git apply`), proposed/ (complete changed files at their repository paths, edited in place so comments survive), imports.tf for objects added from Akeyless, summary.json and the export used.

| Option | Value | Required / default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--repo-url` | REPO_URL | optional | governance repository to clone read-only (GitHub Enterprise HTTPS or SSH URL; uses your git credentials, e.g. `gh auth login --hostname &lt;ghe-host&gt;`) |
| `--repo-dir` | REPO_DIR | optional | existing local checkout to compare (read only, never modified) |
| `--ref` | REF | default main | branch to compare with --repo-url |
| `--model-path` | MODEL_PATH | default terraform/model | model directory inside the repository |
| `--out` | OUT | default reconcile | output directory (replaced; keep it out of Git) |
| `--export-dir` | EXPORT_DIR | optional | use an earlier `watchover export` output instead of exporting now |
| `--from-dir` | FROM_DIR | optional | export offline from a raw/ directory (as `export --from-dir`) |
| `--transport` | cli/api | default cli | how to read Akeyless (as `export`) |
| `--profile` | PROFILE | optional | cli transport: akeyless CLI profile (a read-only identity is enough) |
| `--akeyless` | AKEYLESS | default akeyless | cli transport: path to the akeyless CLI binary |
| `--api` | API | optional | api transport: API URL (default $AKEYLESS_API or https://api.akeyless.io) |
| `--token` | TOKEN | optional | api transport: Akeyless token (default $AKEYLESS_TOKEN) |
| `--only` | ONLY | optional | compare only objects whose name matches this regex |
| `--exclude` | EXCLUDE | repeatable | regex of names to skip (repeatable) |
| `--include-unmodelled` | - | optional | also propose fields set in Akeyless but absent from the model |
| `--propose-removals` | - | optional | propose removing objects that are in the repository but not in Akeyless |

| Environment variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `AKEYLESS_TOKEN` | api transport: token when --token is not given |
| `AKEYLESS_API` | api transport: API URL |

**Exit codes:** 0 no differences; 1 differences found (files written); 2 git, export or model error

```bash
scripts/watchover reconcile --repo-url https://ghe.example.com/platform/akeyless-governance.git --profile akl-readonly
scripts/watchover reconcile --repo-dir ~/src/akeyless-governance --ref main --transport api
scripts/watchover reconcile --repo-dir . --export-dir export/ --out /tmp/reconcile
scripts/watchover reconcile --repo-url git@ghe.example.com:platform/akeyless-governance.git --profile ro --only '^/governance/roles/payments/' --propose-removals
```

<a id="kit-forwarder"></a>
### forwarder

`scripts/watchover forwarder [options]` - Scaffold a new event forwarder (model entry or HCL); --import-existing adopts one by name. *Offline.*

**How it works:**

- Validates name, type, event types, sources and runner with the same rules as the Terraform guards.
- Builds the model entry; secrets become `*_var` keys of TF_VAR_event_forwarder_secrets.
- Prints YAML (default) or HCL; --write inserts the entry into governance.yaml without touching the rest of the file and refuses duplicates; --import-existing adds an import block (ID = name).
- Presets: certificates = certificate-pending-expiration, certificate-expired, certificate-provisioning-success, certificate-provisioning-failure; auth-methods = auth-method-pending-expiration, auth-method-expired, multi-auth-failure, uid-rotation-failure; rotation = next-automatic-rotation, rotated-secret-success, rotated-secret-failure, rotation-usage; secrets = dynamic-secret-failure, static-secret-updated, secret-sync; access-requests = request-access, apply-justification, email-auth-method-approved; operations = gateway-inactive, rate-limiting, usage, usage-report; critical = certificate-expired, certificate-provisioning-failure, auth-method-expired, rotated-secret-failure, dynamic-secret-failure, multi-auth-failure, uid-rotation-failure, gateway-inactive.

| Option | Value | Required / default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--name` | NAME | required | forwarder name, e.g. /governance/events/secops-mail |
| `--type` | email/webhook/slack/teams/service_now | required | forwarder type |
| `--description` | DESCRIPTION | optional | description |
| `--preset` | access-requests/auth-methods/certificates/critical/operations/rotation/secrets | repeatable | add a group of event types (repeatable); the events of each preset are listed under 'How it works' |
| `--event` | EVENT | repeatable | add one event type (repeatable) |
| `--items-source` | ITEMS_SOURCE | repeatable | item path pattern to watch, e.g. '/pki/\*' (repeatable) |
| `--targets-source` | TARGETS_SOURCE | repeatable | target path pattern to watch (repeatable) |
| `--auth-method-source` | AUTH_METHOD_SOURCE | repeatable | auth method path pattern to watch (repeatable) |
| `--gateway-source` | GATEWAY_SOURCE | repeatable | Gateway cluster URL to watch (repeatable; required for teams) |
| `--runner` | immediate/periodic | default immediate | send at once or as a periodic digest |
| `--every` | EVERY | optional | hours between digests (required with --runner periodic) |
| `--disabled` | - | optional | create it disabled |
| `--key` | KEY | optional | protection key for the forwarder's secret (default: account key) |
| `--email-to` | EMAIL_TO | repeatable | email: recipient (repeatable) |
| `--include-error` | - | optional | email: include error details |
| `--override-url` | OVERRIDE_URL | optional | email: Gateway URL used in links (port 18888) |
| `--url` | URL | optional | webhook: URL (slack/teams URLs are secrets and go in the secrets map) |
| `--auth-type` | AUTH_TYPE | optional | webhook: user-pass/bearer-token/certificate; service_now: user-pass/jwt |
| `--username` | USERNAME | optional | webhook: user for user-pass |
| `--host` | HOST | optional | service_now: instance host |
| `--admin-name` | ADMIN_NAME | optional | service_now: admin name (user-pass) |
| `--client-id` | CLIENT_ID | optional | service_now: client ID (jwt) |
| `--user-email` | USER_EMAIL | optional | service_now: user email (jwt) |
| `--format` | yaml/hcl | default yaml | model entry (yaml) or plain resource (hcl) |
| `--write` | GOVERNANCE_YAML | optional | yaml: insert the entry into this governance.yaml |
| `--import-existing` | - | optional | the forwarder already exists in Akeyless: also print the import block (import ID = name) |

**Exit codes:** 0 written; 2 invalid input or duplicate (nothing written)

```bash
scripts/watchover forwarder --name /governance/events/secops-mail --type email --email-to secops@example.com --preset critical --items-source '/*' --auth-method-source '/*'
scripts/watchover forwarder --name /governance/events/pki-slack --type slack --preset certificates --items-source '/pki/*' --write terraform/model/governance.yaml
scripts/watchover forwarder --name /governance/events/siem --type webhook --url https://siem.example.com/akeyless --auth-type bearer-token --preset critical --auth-method-source '/*' --format hcl
scripts/watchover forwarder --name /governance/events/legacy-mail --type email --email-to ops@example.com --event certificate-expired --items-source '/*' --import-existing
```

<a id="kit-conjur"></a>
### conjur

`scripts/watchover conjur [options]` - Translate Conjur policy into model roles + identity bindings. *Offline.*

**How it works:**

- Parses the policy files (!policy, !variable, !host, !layer, !group, !user, !permit, !grant), resolving ids against their policy namespace.
- Maps privileges to capabilities (execute -> read, read -> list, update -> update) on the migrated item paths; one role per layer or group; nested grants are flattened.
- Writes roles/conjur.yaml, bindings.yaml (host/user -> roles, auth method TODO) and REPORT.md.

| Option | Value | Required / default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `policy` | POLICY... | required | Conjur policy YAML files (loaded at the root namespace in the given order) |
| `--item-prefix` | ITEM_PREFIX | default /conjur | Akeyless folder the Gateway migration imports into |
| `--role-prefix` | ROLE_PREFIX | default /governance/roles/ | prefix of the generated Akeyless role names |
| `--out` | OUT | required | output directory (roles/conjur.yaml, bindings.yaml, REPORT.md) |

**Exit codes:** 0 written; 2 unreadable or invalid policy

```bash
scripts/watchover conjur root.yml prod.yml --item-prefix /conjur --out export/conjur
```

<a id="kit-account-settings"></a>
### account-settings

`scripts/watchover account-settings [options]` - Apply account_settings_cli (settings the provider cannot manage) with the CLI. *Live.*

**How it works:**

- Reads account_settings_cli from governance.yaml; rejects unknown flags and keys Terraform manages.
- Builds one `akeyless update-account-settings` call (lists repeat the flag, booleans as =true/false); --dry-run prints it, otherwise runs it with --profile or --token.

| Option | Value | Required / default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--governance` | GOVERNANCE | required | path to model/governance.yaml (reads account_settings_cli) |
| `--profile` | PROFILE | optional | akeyless CLI profile of an account admin |
| `--token` | TOKEN | optional | Akeyless token (default: $AKEYLESS_TOKEN, e.g. from 'watchover token') |
| `--akeyless` | AKEYLESS | default akeyless | path to the akeyless CLI binary |
| `--dry-run` | - | optional | print the update-account-settings command, do not run it |

| Environment variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `AKEYLESS_TOKEN` | token used when --token is not given |

**Exit codes:** 0 applied/printed; 2 invalid settings; else the CLI's exit code

```bash
scripts/watchover account-settings --governance terraform/model/governance.yaml --dry-run
AKEYLESS_TOKEN=$(scripts/watchover token) scripts/watchover account-settings --governance terraform/model/governance.yaml
```

<a id="kit-token"></a>
### token

`scripts/watchover token [options]` - CI: exchange the pipeline JWT for an Akeyless token. *Live.*

**How it works:**

- POSTs {access-id, access-type: jwt, jwt} to <api>/auth and prints the token. No credential is stored.

| Option | Value | Required / default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--api` | API | optional | Akeyless API (default: $AKEYLESS_API or https://api.akeyless.io) |
| `--access-id` | ACCESS_ID | optional | access ID of the CI auth method (default: $AKEYLESS_ACCESS_ID) |
| `--jwt` | JWT | optional | the CI-issued JWT (default: $CI_JWT; prefer the env var - arguments are visible in the process list) |

| Environment variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `AKEYLESS_API` | API base URL |
| `AKEYLESS_ACCESS_ID` | CI auth method access ID |
| `CI_JWT` | CI-issued JWT |

**Exit codes:** 0 token printed; 1 missing settings or authentication failed

```bash
CI_JWT=$JWT AKEYLESS_ACCESS_ID=p-xxxx scripts/watchover token
```

<a id="kit-build-skill"></a>
### build-skill

`scripts/watchover build-skill [options]` - Build the agent-neutral skill package (Agent Skills ZIP) and the prompt pack. *Offline.*

**How it works:**

- Copies SKILL.md (+ agents/ sidecar), docs/*.md as references/ and the kit as template/; validates the result; zips it.
- Writes the prompt pack: full and short system prompt + knowledge files.

| Option | Value | Required / default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--out` | OUT | optional | output directory, replaced (default: dist/ in the kit root) |

**Exit codes:** 0 written; 2 built skill invalid

```bash
scripts/watchover build-skill
scripts/watchover build-skill --out /tmp/wo-dist
```

<a id="kit-install-skill"></a>
### install-skill

`scripts/watchover install-skill [options]` - Install the skill where an AI agent looks for skills (per-agent folders or any folder). *Offline.*

**How it works:**

- Builds the package in a temporary folder and copies it to the agent's skills folder (project or user scope, or --dest). Never overwrites without --force.

| Option | Value | Required / default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--agent` | agents/claude/codex/copilot/cursor/gemini/custom | required | target agent; 'agents' = the shared .agents/skills folder; 'custom' needs --dest |
| `--scope` | project/user | default project | project = inside --project; user = your home directory |
| `--project` | PROJECT | default . | repository the project-scope skill is installed into |
| `--dest` | DEST | optional | explicit skills folder (overrides --agent/--scope) |
| `--force` | - | optional | replace an existing installation |
| `--dry-run` | - | optional | print the target folder, change nothing |

**Exit codes:** 0 installed; 2 target exists (no --force) or custom without --dest

```bash
scripts/watchover install-skill --agent codex --project ../akeyless-governance
scripts/watchover install-skill --agent claude --scope user
scripts/watchover install-skill --agent copilot --project . --dry-run
scripts/watchover install-skill --agent custom --dest ~/my-agent/skills --force
```

<a id="kit-validate-skill"></a>
### validate-skill

`scripts/watchover validate-skill [options]` - Check a skill folder against the Agent Skills specification. *Offline.*

**How it works:**

- Checks SKILL.md: only specification fields; name 1-64 chars, lowercase/digits/hyphens, equal to the folder; description <= 1024; compatibility <= 500; metadata string -> string; body <= 500 lines; every references/*.md it mentions exists.

| Option | Value | Required / default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | PATH | required | skill folder (default: this skill) |

**Exit codes:** 0 valid; 1 problems listed

```bash
scripts/watchover validate-skill
scripts/watchover validate-skill dist/akeyless-watchover
```

<a id="kit-mcp"></a>
### mcp

`scripts/watchover mcp [options]` - Serve the kit, the docs and the skill commands to any MCP client (stdio). *Offline.*

**How it works:**

- JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin/stdout. Tools are generated from each command's options and run `scripts/watchover <command>` in the kit root; output and exit code are returned.
- Resources: SKILL.md, docs, model files. Prompts: one per skill command (skill instructions + request).
- Commands that call Akeyless are listed only with --live.

| Option | Value | Required / default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--repo` | REPO | optional | kit root the tools run in and the model/docs are read from (default: $WATCHOVER_REPO or this repository) |
| `--live` | - | optional | also expose the commands that call Akeyless (same as WATCHOVER_MCP_LIVE=1) |
| `--list` | - | optional | print the tools, resources and prompts, then exit |

| Environment variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `WATCHOVER_MCP_LIVE` | 1 = also expose the commands that call Akeyless (verify, export, account-settings, token) |
| `WATCHOVER_REPO` | kit root the tools run in (default: this repository) |

**Exit codes:** runs until the client closes stdin

```bash
scripts/watchover mcp
WATCHOVER_MCP_LIVE=1 scripts/watchover mcp --repo ~/src/akeyless-governance
```

## Exit codes (all kit commands)

0 success - 1 check failed (mismatch, invalid skill) - 2 usage, input or execution error. Per command: see each entry.
